edge.label: Exfiltrated /etc/shadow or configuration files expose default 'pi' user credentials or system hashes

source_node.label: piSignage Arbitrary File Download via Path Traversal
source_node.precondition: Network access and authenticated low-privilege account on piSignage player API (version < 2.6.4).
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary file disclosure on the Raspberry Pi host (including configuration files, shadow file, and logs) via api/settings/log?file=../.

target_node.label: Raspberry Pi Default Credential Exploitation
target_node.precondition: Network or local access to Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS (<= 5.10) with unchanged default credentials (pi:raspberry).
target_node.postcondition: Authenticated access to the system with 'pi' user privileges and access to sudo/administrative control.

source_evidence.description: The web application component of piSignage before 2.6.4 allows a remote attacker (authenticated as a low-privilege user) to download arbitrary files from the Raspberry Pi via api/settings/log?file=../ path traversal. In other words, this issue is in the player API for log download.

target_node.label: RaspAP Authentication via Recovered/Default Credentials
target_node.precondition: Network access to RaspAP web interface and knowledge of valid or default credentials.
target_node.postcondition: Authenticated session within RaspAP 2.5 web interface.

source_evidence.description: An issue was discovered in includes/webconsole.php in RaspAP 2.5. With authenticated access, an attacker can use a misconfigured (and virtually unrestricted) web console to attack the underlying OS (Raspberry Pi) running this software, and execute commands on the system (including ones for uploading of files and execution of code).

edge.label: Initial code execution provides unprivileged local context on the host to create hard links to log files exploited by OVRRedir.exe

source_node.label: Oculus Browser UI Injection and Code Execution
source_node.precondition: Target user visits a remote malicious web page using Oculus Browser (versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11).
source_node.postcondition: Arbitrary HTML injection into browser UI, UI spoofing, and unprivileged code execution within the Oculus environment.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hard Link Arbitrary File Write
target_node.precondition: Unprivileged local code execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop (< 1.44.0.32849).
target_node.postcondition: Privileged arbitrary file write via hard link to log file, leading to full Local Privilege Escalation (SYSTEM).

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher Handle Leak Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Unprivileged local process execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop (> 1.39 and < 31.1.0.67.507).
target_node.postcondition: Exposure of privileged process handle to unprivileged process, leading to full Local Privilege Escalation (SYSTEM).

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Due to a bug with management of handles in OVRServiceLauncher.exe, an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.
